Name: Pop Girl Spa

Type: AMP

Location: Washington Valley Road, Martinsville, NJ

House fee: $60

Let's just say you wouldn't expect to find an AMP in Martinsville, NJ. Nestled in the wealthy suburbs of Bridgewater and Bedminster, there really shouldn't be any of those houses of corruption and vice in a town were 71% of households are married couples. So, I can't figure out how Pop Girl Spa (PGS) has survived here as long as it has other than it's good at keeping quiet and maybe some palms are being greased. But that's not what I care about, it's about the service, the women and the price.

PGS is an AMP with Chinese management and staff. The spa is off the relatively busy Washington Valley Road which is home to churches, schools and a popular ice cream parlor. You'll need to do a little sleuthing to find it behind what I remember is a hardware or lumber store. The parking is dedicated, off-street and out of sight from passing cars. You'll know the spa is there by the neon "open" sign in the window. Also there's a video camera at the front door which is typical of most AMPs. Generally I've made appointments, but I don't think one is really required here.

The mamasan will greet you as you walk in and you'll notice the spa is fairly new as evidenced by a recent remodel, maybe a couple years old. There are about four rooms, a bathroom and a table shower which is a nice luxury for an AMP in this area. The mamasan will bring you to a room, ask you to undress and your provider will be with you shortly. Now, the providers at PGS are not the young women that I've encountered at the KMPs of Manhattan. It is true these women are from NYC, but it's likely because they are driven in from Flushing or Fort Lee, NJ. That said, I've never had a particularly stunning or shapely provider. They are pedestrian Chinese women that are somewhat generic, but do have a charm about them. It's your cup of tea at the end of the day (I will provide a review of an AMP in the area where the women are a bit of an upgrade).

Your provider will greet you and walk you to the table shower which is also "newish". For me, the TS at PGS has always been a bit clinical, not playful like the KMPs. There isn't as much attention to regions that you'd expect in a more thorough TS. But, it's effective nonetheless and better than showering yourself. I'm a big fan of a playful TS as you can tell from my other reviews.

After the TS, your provider will walk you back to your room. Here is where she will ask for the house fee of $60 and you can choose to tip her in advance here. Now, PGS is a little different from my experience. I believe that standard service is only provided here with nothing extra. Even then, I don't believe that I'd want anything extra at PGS. But, if you want more than standard, likely you can ask and the worst thing she'll do is politely refuse. I've always tipped $60 for standard and sometimes they are very happy about that which means that you might be able to get away with $40 (if you're a cheapskate).

The massage here has always been pretty good. It's likely these women were trained in China or are just very experienced. Unlike a KMP, you'll actually get a massage at PGS. They will know points to hit and even do the backwalk (which I'm not a fan of) on occasion. I'm sure you can direct them to hit certain spots or provide some variance, but it's really up to you. I usually just let the provider roll with whatever they want to do. After a good 25 minutes or so, she'll ask you to flip and she'll massage you for a bit more and then work into the ST. The build-up is usually "okay" as they do a relatively good job in hitting the senses. One thing most providers will not do is get undressed, but they all will let you roam. I think at the end of the day, they want you to be as happy as possible.

After the ST there might be additional massage and a hot towel. The provider will help you get dressed and you'll be on your way.

PGS is a pretty good spot for the beginner and for those who live in the area and don't want to spend a lot of dough. I always went to PGS on a whim, never really planning to go, but without anything better to do I just end up there. Like I say in my guide, the AMP is the hamburger of the spa world... you can get a nice juicy burger for a few bucks but it's not filet minion.

Why i3-gaps over vanilla i3?

Also I really should spin up something that is Wm only.

The gaps between windows help your eyes focus on one specific window (at least for me). It also allows the background to add to the theme. Most of the time you only ever see your background just after booting up, and then you start covering it with windows. Gaps allows it to shine through. It's very pleasing to the eye.

DEs are nice, but a lot of times they are unnecessary. If you're doing an arch setup, installing a DE is basically defeating the point, as it's kind of a bloated set of stuff that you'll only ever use a quarter of it anyway. It's a bit more work getting it set up how you want it, but it tends to be faster and look cleaner.

Posts are divided into different categories (news, event, conflict, diplomacy etc.) based on their content. You can basically do anything, as long as it is based on realism. For example, I could play as Russia, declare war on Ukraine and invade them (this already happened years ago in game), but I couldn't play as India and try and build a moon base in 5 years (this also happened.)

Combat is decided on a roll system. A country will declare war, and then post their assets that they want to send to a certain province. Each then player rolls a 10 sided dice in our IRC, and a round of battle is based on the two numbers they roll, and casualties/equipment damages will be worked out from that roll.
